questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Position?
questions.answer: Position describes where a particle is relative to a chosen origin and coordinate axes. In three-dimensional Cartesian coordinates, the position at time \(t\) is a vector \(\mathbf r(t)\) from the origin to the particle. Displacement compares two positions.

questions.prompt: What does \(O\) mean in Position?
questions.answer: In Position, \(O\) means chosen origin of the coordinate system.

questions.prompt: Identify another important piece of notation used in Position.
questions.answer: In Position, \(t\) means time. Its unit is s.

questions.prompt: A particle moves from \(\mathbf r(1)=2\mathbf i+\mathbf j\) m to \(\mathbf r(4)=-\mathbf i+5\mathbf j\) m. Find its displacement.
questions.answer: Displacement is final position minus initial position. Compute \(\Delta\mathbf r=(-\mathbf i+5\mathbf j)-(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j)=-3\mathbf i+4\mathbf j\) m.

questions.answer: Read the coefficients of the Cartesian basis vectors. The coordinates are \((3,-2,5)\) m relative to the chosen origin.

questions.prompt: Find the displacement from \(\mathbf r_1=\mathbf i+2\mathbf j\) m to \(\mathbf r_2=4\mathbf i-\mathbf j\) m.
questions.answer: Subtract final minus initial: \(\Delta\mathbf r=\mathbf r_2-\mathbf r_1=(4-1)\mathbf i+(-1-2)\mathbf j=3\mathbf i-3\mathbf j\) m.
